issues.description: The problem statement/UML requires a static method SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int), but the solution implements the delivery logic under a different method name: SealSaloon.receiveDelivery(String, int, int). Students following the specification will implement/call acceptSupplyDelivery, while the provided reference solution/API exposes receiveDelivery, leading to mismatched expectations and likely failing tests that look for acceptSupplyDelivery.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution method to match the required API exactly: change `public static void receiveDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity)` to `public static void acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity)` (and update any call sites accordingly).

issues.description: The problem statement instructs students to implement a static shared `stock` for SealSaloon (and mentions initializing it in the constructor), but the provided template Main demonstrates instance-style access (`shop.getStock()`), while the solution exposes `getStock()` as a static method (`public static Stock getStock()`). This inconsistency in how `getStock()` is accessed (instance vs. static) can confuse students and may cause compilation errors if they follow the template call pattern but implement only a static getter (or vice versa).
issues.suggestedFix: Align all artifacts on one access style. If `stock` is meant to be static, either update Main/problem text to use `SealSaloon.getStock()` consistently, or additionally provide an instance getter `public Stock getStock() { return stock; }` (keeping the field static).
